Question: Q2: Which product category (4) has the highest average discount?
Method/Formula: Created a column labelled In_Scope. AVERAGEIFS can only use AND, but we need OR. We use the In_Scope column to label items that have been Shipped, Completed, and Units not blank will be scored 1, and others without will be 0. M column formula: =IF(AND(OR(K2="Shipped",K2="Completed"),G2<>""),1,0). =SUM(M2:M251) was 162. 162 in-scope orders total.
Result: Monitors highest at 5.97%. Software 5.87% (gap 0.10 percentage points); Laptops 5.12%; Accessories 3.55%
Check Performed: AVERAGEIFS matches pivot for all 4 categories (Q2_Check, TRUE for all rows). In-scope count = 162 (170 Shipped/Completed minus 8 blank Units).
Assumptions/Notes: Simple average per order. Shipped/Completed only (Cancelled discounts not realised; Pending discounts may change). Blank-Units orders excluded. Top two categories are close, so the ranking is narrow.

Question: Q2 check: Does a value-weighted average discount change the category ranking?
Method/Formula: Helper columns Clean_Data!N (Gross_Value_GBP, =IF(M2=1,G2*H2,0)) and O (Discount_GBP, =IF(M2=1,N2-L2,0)). Weighted % = SUMIFS(Discount_GBP) ÷ SUMIFS(Gross_Value_GBP) per category (Q2_Check)
Check Performed: Gross − Discount = in-scope revenue (TRUE). Pivot calculated field agrees with formulas.
Assumptions/Notes: Same 162 in-scope orders. Ranking unchanged vs simple average, but Monitors/Software gap shrinks to ~0.01 pp, so treat as a tie at the top

Question: Q3: How does monthly revenue (GBP) trend?
Method/Formula: Helper column Clean_Data!P (Order_Month, =TEXT(B2,"yyyy-mm")). Pivot (Rows: Order_Month; Values: SUM of revenue, Filters: In_Scope = 1). Verified with =SUMIFS(Clean_Data!$L$2:$L$251,Clean_Data!$P$2:$P$251,$A2,Clean_Data!$M$2:$M$251,1)
Result: Peak: Aug (£27,215.40). Lowest: Jun (£10,143.73). Sales dipped low in May and lowest in June, climbing to the peak in August and then averaging out in September/October.
Check Performed: SUMIFS matches pivot for all 10 months; monthly total equals Q1 total (£183,038.99)
Assumptions/Notes: Shipped/Completed only. Data ends 27/10/2026, so October is a partial month (understated). Pending orders may later be cancelled or shipped

Question: Q4: Which sales rep has completed the most orders?
Method/Formula: Pivot (Rows: Sales Rep; Values: COUNTA of Order ID; Filter: Status = Completed). Verified with =COUNTIFS(Clean_Data!$J$2:$J$251,$A2,Clean_Data!$K$2:$K$251,B$1) in Q4_Check
Result: Daniel Evans and Priya Shah tied on 8. Sophie Turner 7; Aisha Khan 5; Tom Hargreaves 4; Liam O’Connor 3
Check Performed: COUNTIFS matches pivot for all 6 named reps. 35 named + 3 Unassigned = 38 total Completed orders
Assumptions/Notes: Completed status only (question-specific; differs from revenue rule). In_Scope flag not applied, as this counts orders, not revenue. “Unassigned” (3 Completed orders) excluded from ranking. Tie reported, not broken. Q4 counts orders so blank units are included if completed. 10 orders are unassigned, of which 3 are completed. A tie-break (e.g. revenue from Completed orders) can be added if the data owner requests one.
